title: Indian Railways Freight Loading (Monthly)
description: Total revenue-earning freight originating on Indian Railways each month, in million tonnes, as announced by the Ministry of Railways in monthly press releases carried by PIB. Rail moves coal, iron ore, steel, cement, foodgrains, fertiliser, containers and petroleum, so loading is a timely volume read on mining, power, construction and manufacturing activity - available about two weeks after month-end, months before the IIP. It is a volume series (not revenue) and complements the older Railway Freight Traffic - Revenue page, which stops in Dec 2024.
source: Ministry of Railways, monthly press releases (via PIB)

qna.question: What does freight loading measure?
qna.answer: Million tonnes of revenue-earning goods loaded (originating) on Indian Railways in the month. Coal is about half of the total, followed by iron ore, cement and clinker, foodgrains, fertiliser, steel, containers and POL.

qna.question: How should I read it?
qna.answer: Use year-on-year growth: loading is seasonal (monsoon months are weaker for coal and iron ore; Q4 and March are strong). Coal loading tracks power demand and mine output; containers, steel and cement track construction and manufacturing demand.^Rail loading has been rising in structural steps (dedicated freight corridors), so growth rates run above those of industrial output.

qna.question: What are the caveats?
qna.answer: The data come from monthly press releases whose wording and commodity detail vary, and some months were never announced, so the series has gaps. Loading counts tonnes at origin only, and revisions in Railway Board's final statistics can differ slightly from the figures announced.

note: Not every month has a monthly press release, so the series has gaps (no values are filled or interpolated). Where a release states the same month of the previous year, that year-ago figure is also used. Figures are those announced in the releases and may differ slightly from later Railway Board statistics.
